$comment: docs/risk-tiers.md is the source; this file restates its tier table as data. scripts/check-policies.mjs fails when the two disagree (tier number, name, paths, required commands, scrutiny), and when a floor path leaves the highest tier. Tier 2 is the MOST dangerous tier. A path matching several tiers takes the highest. There is no human merge gate on any tier: agent pull requests auto-merge once the required check `test` passes, and the owner's brakes are the `hold` label and pausing the repository in the hive. Scrutiny says how hard the reviewer agent looks and what the pull request must state, not who merges. A path glob cannot see inside a file, so a reviewer may raise a tier above the path match, never lower it.

brakes: hold label on the pull request
pause the repository in the hive

tiers.name: tooling
pr_must_state: which required commands ran and what they printed
for a workflow: what was verified and what cannot be until it runs (a schedule, a secret)
for a policy or risk-config change: whether it loosens a rule

tiers.name: live
pr_must_state: machine impact: what reaches enrolled machines, and when (next timer run, next recreate)
whether unit files changed, so each machine needs systemctl --user daemon-reload
for an ini change that depends on the image: that the image change is already on main with a green build
that no proprietary app is baked into the image
how it was tested without touching a real apps box
